title: Monoidal flat model for unbounded complexes on a ringed site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Write $\mathcal A_R=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ for its category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal A_R)$ for its unbounded cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Here a combinatorial differential graded model category means a locally presentable category enriched, tensored and cotensored over unbounded complexes of abelian groups (with cochain differentials and quasi-isomorphisms as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]), with cofibrations, fibrations and weak equivalences satisfying two-out-of-three, closure under retracts, and functorial factorizations into (cofibration, trivial fibration) and (trivial cofibration, fibration), with the corresponding lifting properties. The two weak factorization systems are generated by sets. Enrichment satisfies the model compatibility axiom: for a cofibration $i$ and a fibration $p$, the induced map of Hom complexes is a fibration in the projective model structure on complexes of abelian groups, trivial if $i$ or $p$ is trivial. Trivial means also a weak equivalence. Stable means that the enhanced localization has a zero object and finite homotopy limits and colimits, and its homotopy pushout squares are exactly its homotopy pullback squares. A differential graded Quillen adjunction is an enriched adjunction whose left adjoint preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. Its enhanced localization retains derived mapping complexes and all composition homotopies; equivalently one may use the associated stable homotopy theory with its chain enrichment when the model category is stable.

There is a stable combinatorial differential graded model structure on $\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal A_R)$ whose weak equivalences are exactly the quasi-isomorphisms and whose cofibrations are exactly the termwise monomorphisms with K-flat, termwise flat cokernel [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Thus its cofibrant objects are exactly the K-flat complexes with flat terms. Its ordinary homotopy category is the unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal A_R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and the complex of internal sheaf Homs [def-pur-sheaf-hom] give a closed symmetric monoidal model structure: the tensor unit $R[0]$ is cofibrant, the pushout product of two cofibrations is a cofibration, and it is trivial if either factor is trivial. Here closed means tensor in each variable has the internal-Hom right adjoint; the complex of internal Homs has degree $r$ equal to $\prod_p\mathcal Hom_R(P^p,Q^{p+r})$ and differential $h\mapsto d_Qh-(-1)^rh d_P$. Fibrations and the two functorial factorizations are part of the asserted model structure; no enough-projectives hypothesis or flatness assumption on a later coefficient homomorphism is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution) supplies K-flat flat-term replacements only. The model-structure, factorization, enrichment and monoidal assertions here are additional agent-formulated foundations, not the content of that tag. WANTED: a flat-model-structure reference for module sheaves on arbitrary small ringed sites.

proof.text: By [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], $\mathcal A_R$ is Grothendieck abelian. Its complex category is also Grothendieck: kernels, cokernels and colimits are taken degreewise, so filtered colimits remain exact. If $G$ is a generator of $\mathcal A_R$, the disks $D^nG$ (copies of $G$ in degrees $n,n+1$, differential identity) form a generating family, since $\operatorname{Hom}(D^nG,X)=\operatorname{Hom}(G,X^n)$; their coproduct over $n\in\mathbf Z$ is a generator. These observations verify exactly the definition [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], without assuming projectives.

source.place: Tags 03DA, 03DB, 03EW: colimits, exact filtered colimits, generator; degreewise extension to complexes is the displayed elementary argument.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-flat-complex-cotorsion-pairs] on the given small site and ring sheaf. Adopt its classes $\mathcal D,\mathcal E,\mathcal E_0,\mathcal W$: $\mathcal D$ is exactly flat-term K-flat, $\mathcal W$ is acyclic, $\mathcal E_0=\mathcal E\cap\mathcal W$, and the two asserted cotorsion pairs are complete and small. The acyclic class is closed under retracts because cohomology respects retracts. It is thick by the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact]. Thus the triple $(\mathcal D,\mathcal W,\mathcal E)$ meets every hypothesis of model recognition.

source.place: Agent argument supplying the additional flat-model foundation before the derived coefficient adjunction; the two cotorsion pairs are a separate open theorem, not inferred from Tag 06YS.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-small-cotorsion-model-recognition] to the complex category in Step 1 and the triple from Step 2. This gives a combinatorial model structure with the required cofibrations and with fibrations the epimorphisms with kernel in $\mathcal E$. Its weak equivalences are precisely quasi-isomorphisms: a trivial cofibration and a trivial fibration have acyclic cokernel and kernel, respectively, so are quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact], as is their composite. Conversely, factor any quasi-isomorphism $f=pi$ by the supplied cofibration/trivial-fibration factorization. Since $p$ is already a quasi-isomorphism, so is $i$; its long exact sequence makes its cokernel acyclic. This cokernel is in $\mathcal D\cap\mathcal W$, so $i$ is trivial. The same recognition theorem supplies functorial factorizations and sets generating both weak factorization systems. Applying the cofibration description to $0\to P$ identifies the cofibrant objects as exactly $\mathcal D$.

source.place: Agent verification of the weak equivalences and cofibrant objects for the flat-model presentation used in proof paragraph 2.

proof.text: Use the tensor--sheaf-Hom adjunction and symmetric monoidal structure of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. On complexes take the direct-sum tensor of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and the product Hom of [def-pur-hom-complex]. A degree-zero cochain map $P\otimes Q\to T$ is the family of maps $P^p\otimes Q^q\to T^{p+q}$ obeying its differential equation. Transpose each component by the sheaf adjunction with the Koszul sign: for $x\in P^p$, $y\in Q^q$, set $g(y)(x)=(-1)^{pq}t(x\otimes y)$. The chain-map equation for $t$ gives $d_{\mathcal Hom}(g(y))(x)=(-1)^{pq+p}t(x\otimes d_Qy)=g(d_Qy)(x)$, exactly the equation for a cochain map $Q\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,T)$. Direct-sum and product universal properties give inverse natural bijections. Associativity, unit and signed symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{|x||y|}y\otimes x$ follow componentwise from those for module sheaves; their coherence equations hold on every summand. In particular this is the actual closed tensor and the precise internal-Hom formula asserted in the item.

source.place: Tag 03EO (lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor); direct-sum/product totalization and the written differential calculation.

proof.text: For $C,D\in\mathcal D$, the terms of $C\otimes D$ are flat: tensoring two flat modules composes their exact tensor functors, and a countable direct sum is flat by [lem-pc-kflat-closure]. It is K-flat directly from [def-pc-kflat-complex]: if $N$ is acyclic, $N\otimes C$ is acyclic, hence $(N\otimes C)\otimes D$ is acyclic, and Step 4 identifies this with $N\otimes(C\otimes D)$. If $C$ or $D$ is also acyclic, [lem-pur-acyclic-kflat-tensor-arbitrary] says $C\otimes D$ is acyclic, without any boundedness condition on the other factor. Thus $\mathcal D$ is tensor-closed and its acyclic part is a tensor ideal among cofibrant objects.

source.place: Definition 06YN and the acyclic K-flat tensor property; associativity and flatness calculations are written out here.

proof.text: Let $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ and $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be cofibrations, and write $C=B/A$, $D=Y/X$. Their degreewise cokernels are flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-quotient-tensor-ses], both short exact sequences remain exact after tensoring with any module sheaf. In each bidegree this gives $(A\otimes Y)\cap(B\otimes X)=A\otimes X$ inside $B\otimes Y$: quotient by $A\otimes Y$ identifies the images with $C\otimes X\subseteq C\otimes Y$, and the kernel in $B\otimes X$ is $A\otimes X$. Consequently the map from the pushout $(B\otimes X)\coprod_{A\otimes X}(A\otimes Y)$ into $B\otimes Y$ is monic, with quotient $C\otimes D$. Take the direct sum over bidegrees of fixed total degree. Such sums preserve these exact sequences, since they are filtered colimits of finite sums in the Grothendieck category of Step 1. The maps respect the total differential, so the pushout product is a termwise monomorphism of complexes with cokernel exactly $C\otimes D$. Step 5 makes it a cofibration, trivial if $i$ or $j$ is trivial, since Step 3 identifies triviality with acyclicity of the respective cokernel.

source.place: Tags 03EX (lemma-flat-tor-zero), 03EY (lemma-flat-ses); the intersection and quotient computation is the explicit elementary pushout-product argument.

proof.text: The unit module $R$ is flat because $R\otimes_R-$ is the identity. The complex $R[0]$ is bounded above and flat-term, so [lem-pc-kflat-closure] makes it K-flat. It is therefore cofibrant by Step 3. Steps 4--6 prove the closed symmetric monoidal model axioms with this cofibrant unit. These arguments apply to arbitrary small ringed sites, including ones without enough points; all exactness used is exactness of sheaves. They do not impose any flatness on a coefficient homomorphism.

source.place: Bounded-flat K-flatness (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat); the unit computation is elementary.

proof.text: The dg enrichment has $\operatorname{Hom}^{r}(P,Q)=\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_R}(P^n,Q^{n+r})$ with the same differential as Step 4 and componentwise composition. It is tensored and cotensored over complexes of abelian groups as follows. For an abelian group $V$ presented by $\mathbf Z^{(J)}\to\mathbf Z^{(I)}\to V\to0$, form $V\odot M$ as the corresponding cokernel of coproducts of $M$, and its right adjoint $M^V$ as the kernel of $\prod_I M\to\prod_J M$. The cokernel and kernel universal properties give $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_R}(V\odot M,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf{Ab}}(V,\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_R}(M,N))$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_R}(N,M^V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf{Ab}}(V,\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_R}(N,M))$, naturally in all variables; hence these objects are independent of the presentation. For a complex $K$ use $(K\odot P)^r=\bigoplus_{a+b=r}K^a\odot P^b$ and $(P^K)^r=\prod_a(P^{a+r})^{K^a}$, with differentials $d(k\odot x)=d_Kk\odot x+(-1)^a k\odot d_Px$ for $k\in K^a$, and $(df)^a=d_Pf^a-(-1)^rf^{a+1}d_K$ for a homogeneous $f$ of degree $r$. The presentation, direct-sum and product universal properties identify maps with the corresponding families of abelian-group maps and give the enriched tensor/cotensor adjunctions. Expanding the differential gives $d^2=0$, and $d(gf)=d(g)f+(-1)^{|g|}g d(f)$. Thus this is a dg category with all the stated tensors and cotensors, using the limits and colimits established in Step 1.

source.place: Agent construction of the external chain enrichment required before the finite derived mapping calculation; formulas reduce the claims to the universal properties of sums, products, kernels and cokernels.

proof.text: For a cofibration $i:A\to B$ and a fibration $p:X\to Y$, put $C=\operatorname{coker}i\in\mathcal D$ and $T=\ker p\in\mathcal E$. By [lem-coef-flat-complex-cotorsion-pairs] each $T^m$ is cotorsion. In every pair of degrees, a square against $i^n,p^m$ has obstruction an extension of $C^n$ by $T^m$: form the pullback of $p^m$ along $B^n\to Y^m$ and quotient by the specified lift from $A^n$. This gives $0\to T^m\to E\to C^n\to0$, which splits since $C^n$ is flat. A splitting gives the required graded filler. Choosing fillers in all degrees shows the map of abelian-group Hom complexes $\operatorname{Hom}(B,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,X)\times_{\operatorname{Hom}(A,Y)}\operatorname{Hom}(B,Y)$ is degreewise surjective, with kernel $\operatorname{Hom}(C,T)$. If $i$ is trivial, $C\in\mathcal D\cap\mathcal W$ and the definition of $\mathcal E$ in the cited theorem makes this kernel acyclic. If $p$ is trivial, $T\in\mathcal E_0$ and its defining property makes the kernel acyclic for every $C\in\mathcal D$. In the projective model on abelian-group complexes, a fibration means a degreewise surjection, and a trivial fibration means a degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism. Thus the Hom map is a fibration. In either trivial case its degreewise short exact kernel sequence and [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact], applied in $\mathbf{Ab}$, make it a quasi-isomorphism, hence a trivial fibration. This proves the precise dg compatibility axiom; no sectionwise surjectivity of an epimorphism of sheaves was assumed.

source.place: Agent verification of chain enrichment compatibility from the two cotorsion pairs; global module Hom is distinguished from internal sheaf Hom. The projective-fibration terminology is used in its defining sense of degreewise surjections, trivial when also quasi-isomorphisms; the quasi-isomorphism conclusion uses the cited long exact sequence in abelian groups.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-pointed-model-stability] for the model category of Step 3. The zero complex is a zero object. Its ordinary homotopy category is the localization at the quasi-isomorphisms, hence is $D(\mathcal A_R)$ by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. To verify stability, take a cofibrant $P$ and $CP=\operatorname{Cone}(1_P)$, with $CP^n=P^n\oplus P^{n+1}$ and differential $(x,y)\mapsto(d_Px+y,-d_Py)$. The inclusion $P\to CP$ is a cofibration with cokernel $P[1]$: shifts preserve flat terms and K-flatness directly, and cones are K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-closure]. The cone is contractible, with contraction $(x,y)\mapsto(0,x)$, so $CP\to0$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Replace both zero legs of the suspension span by this inclusion. All three objects are cofibrant and both maps are cofibrations, so the cited generic theorem computes the homotopy pushout by $CP\coprod_P CP$. The natural quotient to the second copy modulo $P$, namely $P[1]$, has kernel the first copy $CP$, hence is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact]. The construction is natural in $P$. It identifies derived suspension with $[1]$, whose inverse is $[-1]$ on $D(\mathcal A_R)$. The suspension criterion therefore gives stability of the enhanced localization, including equivalence of homotopy pushout and homotopy pullback squares. After stability has been established, apply [lem-coef-dg-derived-quillen-calculus] to this stable combinatorial differential graded model category and its identity enriched Quillen adjunction. Its functorial cofibrant/fibrant replacement description supplies the derived mapping complexes and their coherent composition in the enhanced localization, as required by the introductory enhancement convention. Together with Steps 3--9 this proves every clause of the item.

source.place: Agent cone computation of suspension and application of the generic coherent stability criterion; this is stronger than merely noting the triangulated ordinary derived category. The retained derived mapping complexes and coherent composition are supplied by the existing generic dg derived Quillen calculus, applied only after stability is proved.
